content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, licence scope).**

**What I checked**
- **Section 2 (Grant of Rights)**: the hosting licence (2.1) is "perpetual and irrevocable"; the internal-use licence (2.2) is "royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual"; sublicensing to an unlimited number of Customers and Software Users is expressly permitted, and 2.4 adds distribution rights. No revocability-at-will problem, so this is nowhere near walk-away territory.
- **Section 14.1 (Assignment)**: assignment permitted without consent in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all related assets (competitor carve-out only) — this satisfies the fallback on successor transfer, and each grant's "nontransferable" is expressly qualified by reference to 14.1.
- **Definitions**: "Affiliate" appears nowhere in the Agreement; "contractor"/"subcontractor" also absent. "Corio Servers" ("owned or operated by or for Corio") only partially reaches contractor operation.

**Why it deviates**: the rule's fallback requires affiliates to be covered (at minimum on written notice). Here affiliates and contractors are neither named nor addable via any mechanism, which is a material failure of the fallback on the one element the rule is built around.

**Redline (validated ok:true)**: a single new Section 2.11 extending all Section 2 licences to Corio's affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf, with Corio responsible for their compliance — the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position, with the written-notice fallback offered in the comment. Transferability and irrevocability were left untouched as already compliant.
